runtime_budget.cleanup_mechanism: Recurring background job in services/telemetry/main.py runs every 300s (PANTHEON_TELEMETRY_HEARTBEAT_RETENTION_INTERVAL_SECONDS) and deletes public.telemetry_events rows of event_type='infrastructure_health' older than PANTHEON_TELEMETRY_INFRA_HEALTH_RETENTION_DAYS (default 7) in bounded 5,000-row batches under a 15,000ms statement timeout, subject to ingested_seq <= min_consumer_checkpoint_seq and excluding all event IDs referenced by incidents or postmortems.

retention_job_contract.safe_sequence_ceiling: min(trade_journey_projection.controller.checkpoint_seq) across all registered controllers; refuses to delete when checkpoint is missing or <= 0

readers.rationale: Point lookup by event_id via TelemetryIngestService.get_accepted_event (in-memory hot store + PostgreSQL fallback build_postgres_event_reader). Referenced incident/postmortem event IDs are excluded from deletion indefinitely.

LineageReadService.query('telemetry_event_trace') resolves event_id from in-memory admitted events, PostgreSQL event_reader, or _svc.get_accepted_event fallback in _lineage_query_response. Referenced incident/postmortem event IDs remain resolvable without conflict markers.

When is_infrastructure_health_incident(parent_incident) is true, validate_postmortem validates trace_id and telemetry_event_ids (stripping merged_event:<incident_id>: prefixes) against telemetry_service.get_accepted_event for event_type == 'infrastructure_health'. All event IDs referenced by any incident or postmortem record are protected from deletion.

InfrastructureHealthIncidentConsumer consumes real-time/outbox infrastructure_health event payloads directly on emission without calling CanonicalReferenceValidator.validate_incident, and records source_event_id into trace_id and telemetry_event_ids on the resulting incident case.

ResolvedIncidentPostmortemDraftConsumer creates/updates postmortem drafts from resolved incident envelopes without calling CanonicalReferenceValidator.validate_incident, copying trace_id and telemetry_event_ids into the postmortem record.
Maintains local SQLite incident_mappings (opening_event_id, last_event_id) and delivery_outbox (source_event_id) and delivers real-time/outbox probes to telemetry and incidents.
infrastructure_health is not in LIFECYCLE_EVENT_TYPES and is ignored once ingested_seq <= trade_journey_projection.controller.checkpoint_seq; retention never deletes rows above min(checkpoint_seq).

sources_inspected: PostgreSQL incident.incident_cases (payload JSONB: trace_id, telemetry_event_ids including merged_event:<incident_id>:<event_id>, source_event_id, opening_event_id, last_event_id, and source_event_id=<id> in evidence_summary)
PostgreSQL incident.postmortems (payload JSONB: trace_id, telemetry_event_ids including merged_event:<incident_id>:<event_id>, source_event_id)
Optional JSON store at INCIDENT_STORE_PATH (incidents and postmortems dictionaries/lists)
Optional BFF SQLite state DB at PANTHEON_DOWNSTREAM_HEALTH_STATE_PATH (incident_mappings.opening_event_id, incident_mappings.last_event_id, delivery_outbox.source_event_id)
reference_protection_mechanism.why_payload_incident_ref_is_not_used_as_: In services/control-plane/bff/downstream_health_monitor.py (:3036-3055), _store.get_incident(target_name) returns the incident_mappings row even after its status is 'resolved', so every subsequent healthy probe for that target carries payload.incident_ref. Filtering on payload->>'incident_ref' IS NULL would retain all future healthy probes for that target forever. Protecting the exact event IDs referenced by incident/postmortem stores and active outbox/mappings retains all incident and postmortem evidence (~2-8 rows per incident) while allowing unreferenced probes older than 7 days to be deleted.
reference_protection_mechanism.consume_infrastructure_health_validation: Confirmed: POST /api/incidents/consume-infrastructure-health (services/incidents/main.py:606) delegates to InfrastructureHealthIncidentConsumer.consume_infrastructure_health_event (services/incidents/consumer.py:482), which does not call CanonicalReferenceValidator.validate_incident. Similarly, POST /api/postmortems/consume-resolved-incident (services/postmortems/main.py:369) delegates to ResolvedIncidentPostmortemDraftConsumer (services/postmortems/consumer.py:216) without calling CanonicalReferenceValidator.validate_incident. Manual postmortem validation in CanonicalReferenceValidator.validate_postmortem (services/incident/reference_validation.py:345) checks is_infrastructure_health_incident(parent_incident) and resolves trace_id and telemetry_event_ids via telemetry_service.get_accepted_event.

residual_findings.description: POST /api/postmortems (manual postmortem creation) calls reference_validator.validate_incident(parent_incident) unconditionally before validate_postmortem(record, parent_incident=parent_incident). Because validate_incident does not branch on is_infrastructure_health_incident(record) before checking RuntimeManager for runtime_id/deployment_id, manual POST /api/postmortems for a non-trading infrastructure incident (which uses synthetic runtime_id='infra-subject-...' and deployment_id='infra-deployment-...') fails RuntimeBinding validation. Automated postmortem creation via POST /api/postmortems/consume-resolved-incident is unaffected.
residual_findings.disposition: Out of scope for TELEMETRY-INFRA-HEALTH-RETENTION-20261117 (scoped to services/telemetry/* and scripts/*); recorded as residual finding for coordinator attachment to problem register.
